elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Section 11.1 expressly permits Customer to terminate the Agreement for convenience during the Term.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: Customer must provide at least 90 days' written notice, exceeding 30 days.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: No pro-rata refund of prepaid fees is required; instead, Customer must pay an early-termination fee and other specified amounts.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: M&I's withdrawal of non-Core Services may become effective only at the end of the Term. The separate immediate-termination language is tied to regulatory, legislative, or judicial action, not convenience.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Section 11.1 permits Customer to terminate for convenience upon at least 90 days' written notice.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: The Termination for Convenience Fee, together with all other amounts payable under Section 11.1, may not exceed three months' fees.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: M&I's withdrawal of non-Core Services is expressly effective only at the end of the Term.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: M&I must provide 90 days' prior written notice before its end-of-Term withdrawal of non-Core Services.
